While it is certainly not as popular as deep learning models like LLMs, it certainly suggests other useful mechanisms. Chiefly, I think that the way MLNs behave might be able to model the “collapse of the wave function” phenomenon on a completely software basis, with no need for a physical mechanism like quantum effects. Of course this is a long shot by me and might be completely wrong, but who knows? Even if MLNs do not solve intelligence, they could solve the problem of consciousness. In any case, MLNs are proposed by the author to use gradient descent or even genetic algorithms( without cross-over) as the optimization functions to be used, but would the parameters be as learnable and compress information as good as the weights of a deep learning model do ? My answer is no. A highly connectionist approach seems like the most efficient way to compress information and accurately learn new things based on any training data used, far better than the other 4 approaches. I am ready to bet on deep learning to be the key to solve the problem of AGI. However, consciousness is a different matter, one that still has no possible valid explanations currently in the software world. Let’s see if that changes in future.

posts.title: The intersection of modern physics, math, and consciousness, and a new view of AGI
posts.summary: My thoughts on Roger Penrose’s book “The Emperor’s New Mind”
posts.html:
This blog contains my writings on my opinions and thoughts on Roger Penrose’s viewpoint of consciousness as he descibes in his book: ” The Emperor’s New Mind”, his sequel book : ” Shadows of the mind”, and his videos on youtube as well. All his ideas have a direct relation to the limits of computation, intelligence, and therefore, future existence of AGI or a self-improving superintelligence, which is why I am very interested in this specific perspective. Again, I do not always write about books I have read, but this topic begs a lot of further discussion because it holds the key to inventing AGI.

Firstly, a bit of introduction: Sir Roger Penrose OM FRS HonFInstP is a British mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He has contributed to the mathematical physics of general relativity and cosmology. He has received several prizes and awards, including the 1988 Wolf Prize in Physics, which he shared with Stephen Hawking for the Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems, and the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics “for the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity”. As he describes in his words, during his research and study days he attended 3 main courses( or study directions) , which were: theory of general relativity, quantum mechanics, and lastly, theory of computation. The latter one has no connection( seemingly) to the others, and consists of computability, complexity, turing machines, study of algorithms and their limitations, and also has foundations in mathematics ( Godel’s theorem). All of these subjects are important to this article.

Penrose holds the opinion that consciousness is not a computation. A computation can be described as a mechanization, or a process whereby an algorithm( specific set of instructions) gives an output when tasked with something, or given an input. The strong-AI viewpoint says that intelligence and consciousness consist of algorithmic components, and that human thinking is essentially a computational process( hence all things like imagination, creativity, perception, feelings, intuition and so on , are a direct result of complex computations carried out by our neurons with the help of some unknown algorithm). I myself am a firm believer of the strong-AI viewpoint. However, Penrose says that consciousness is a non-algorithmic process, and hence no algorithm or computer is capable of achieving human thinking.

First of all , why even bother with consciousness ? Why to worry about emulating consciousness on a computer, when we already have superb AI systems that possess specialized, or even general, intelligence? If we were to invent an AGI, is consciousness even necessary for it ? My answer is YES, consciousness is a MUST, because without it, we have nothing more than a very intelligent system that has no awareness of itself or its thinking process, and this has serious limitations. In short, for any superintelligence to work( in favour of humans, under our AI alignment for human goals) , and eventually surpass humans, it must possess consciousness.

In his book, he descibes in beautiful detail, concepts like Turing machines, computations and algorithms, Godel’s incompleteness theorem, recursion and recursive sets and recursively enumerable sets in math, as well as a long trip to Galileo’s and Einstein’s relativistic world, the quantum world, cosmology, and time. The last chapter also wonderfully describes the human brain, its workings, and even some brain experiments with mysterious unexplained observed results, and also varying degrees of consciousness in other animals . In short, it is a wonderful( yet might be tedious and filled with math jargon for other people) book, and is a must-read for anyone deeply interested in AGI and the future of computers., and especially inclined towards physics and math. Via this book, he describes how,in his viewpoint, consciousness is a fundamentally non-algorithmic process, and that further, it must be explainable via quantum mechanics. He states that even in today’s world( as of 2024), we lack the physics needed to explain consciousness, and that further progress in physics is greatly needed to solve all mysteries. I agree with this last statement a lot, we still need to discover new physics that can explain how human thinking takes place. Yet I also disagree with some of Penrose’s points, but more on that later on.

Basically , this all traces back to how Godel’s incompleteness theorem works. For more detail on this, refer to my previous blog on this subject( “GEB book by Douglas Hofstadter”). The way Godel’s theorem points out the inherent limitations in mathematics, that it is inconsistent and incomplete, has a direct effect on the way how Turing machines are in turn described. Alan Turing introduced a fantastic way to represent the very fundamental way to describe computation, via Turing machines. Yet for all their power, they are mechanizations, and they represent algorithmic processes, and all algorithms have an inherent limitation: using the axioms of the mathmatical system( the algorithm steps), the algorithm can never say for sure that it will ever terminate(or run on in a loop till infinity) ( this is where concepts like P vs NP problems of computational complexity come into consideration). Hofstadter, in his book, says that the way Godel proved this limitation in his theorem was ingenious, and that this method is the key to consciousness and intelligence ( self-referential systems, or strange loops as he describes). However, Penrose points out some valid flaws in this theory, stating that if that were the case, even Godel numbers themselves would therefore be conscious! Which, as any sane person would agree, is nonsensical : numbers cannot be conscious, they are abstract concepts. Even though Hofstadter’s theory might be right in some regard, it definitely has its own flaws. In any case, Penrose says that even if the axioms leading up to the limitations in formal systems are limited, we as humans CAN clearly see whether the resulting computation will terminate or not, hence essentially we have the ability to surpass, or “transcend” the limitations of mathematics and algorithmic processes via our own methods, and this is the reason which he believes is why , indirectly, Godel’s theorem shows us that human thinking might not be a computation.

Penrose then goes on to describe concepts like Mandelbrot set, and how recursion occurs in its graph, yet that recursion itself has some mysterious qualities ( the kind of things you will encounter if you study complex numbers , and recursive sets and recursively enumerable sets). Via his description, he explains how mathematics itself has an inherent beauty and “timelessness” that sets it apart from normal arts and sciences invented by humans. He also points out the difference between determinism and non-computability: some process might be deterministic(meaning it is not random and has a predictable flow to it), yet in the end it might ultimately turn out to be non-computable, essentially rendering it to be something that can never be carried out by a computer. This falls under Hamiltonian mechanics, and the phase space descibed by such a dynamical system, that can be conceptualized under Classical Mechanics. Yet, over the course of evolution of a Hamiltonian system, if one were to simulate it or track its end form using an algorithm, they will fall short and find out that computation is not sufficient for this, that some non-algorithmic process is involved here.

But what does this have to do with human brains and consciousness? Well , since there is no current physics that can accurately describe human thinking, Penrose suggests that quantum mechanics is involved in the play. If the reader is familiar with Schrodinger’s wave equation and its implications, he will understand the following : the evolution of the wave function, over a superposition of states, undergoes a complete “collapse of the wave function”. This phenomenon is the very reason why quantum mechanics falls short of our real world, meaning that quantum mechanics itself is incomplete. Penrose puts forth his theorem to explain consciousness in the human brain: ” ORCH OR “, or Orchestrated Objective-Reduction.

Objective-reduction refers to the collapse of the wave function , and ‘orchestrated’ refers to a unison in this phenomenon. Basically, his hypothesis proposes that there exist microtubules in our brains( tiny structures with a certain geometrical symmetry) which exhibit quantum-mechanical effects such that this system spreads out over a wide area of microtubules spanning numerous neurons at one point in time, and via the collapse of the wave function that happens, conciousness emerges. It is proven under some recent experiments that anaesthesia molecules directly affect those regions of the brain where microtubule activity is shown to have been lowered, hence further proving that there might be some valid connection between consciousness and microtubules. The geometrical symmetry shown by microtubules also has a certain connection to quasicrystals that show the “forbidden” five-fold symmetry in nature, which can only be explained via quantum mechanics: the five-fold symmetry is achieved via evolution of Schrodinger’s equation over a superposition of probable outcomes, and ultimately one of those worlds is chosen when collapse of the wave function occurs. Now this process is certainly non-algorthmic: it cannot be mechanized, and it therefore cannot be described by a Turing machine, hence never by a computer.

Namely, Penrose says that his Orch OR theory i dependent on THAT part of quantum mechanics which is incomplete, which causes discrepancy between our real classical world, and the quantum world. His theory is controversial in the scientific community, but I would not be so quick to dismiss it, there might be relevant truths to be understood from it.

Other descriptions of consciousness as given by others hint at it being derived from human language. Yet Broca’s region, the part of brain that processes language, cannot fully explain how consciousness works. Nor can we say for sure how different the cerebellum works as compared to the cerebral cortex, with one explanation by Penrose stating that our cerebellum acts like an automaton, hence not requiring consciousness, and the cerebral part has a mysterious component to it, hence requiring quantum-mechanical effects. What if, according to one of my own views, the microtubules affect the synaptic strengths of neurons over an area, hence physically affecting them in a ” patterned manner” , in such a way that : the establishment of self-referential loops between the globally coherent microtubules, and the neural synaptic strengths they affect, be the truth behind consciousness ? In such viewpoint, both Penrose and Hofstadter would find common ground to agree, with this phenomenon following certain patterns and forming self-referential loops on a higher level. Even the viewpoint of Digital Physics might, I believe, prove useful, where the very notion of “information” itself is more fundamental than atoms in this universe.

Ultimately, even Penrose admits he doesn’t know the full story. There are far too many unknown factors into play here. Some of his views on Plato’s world of mathematics, as well as his other ideas, do not sound accurate to me, and I believe there exist other explanations to those ideas which might be more accurate( one of them being that, rather than 2 mathematicians discussing some math concept come at a common understanding of the concept without use of a sensible communication or descriptive language, and it being the consequence of Plato’s world or some abstract inexplicable entity, what happens could be as simple as efficient information compression via different representations on a high-level abstraction( kind of like what happens in an autoencoder model , so essentially 2 humans employ 2 different ways of representing an idea, and compress that information in an efficient, yet non-communicable manner. While his overall idea that he wants to convey is certainly worth thinking about, there are some aspects that he misses, and I do not agree with some of his beliefs.

After reading his book, I myself am unsure about what to believe or think. I might feel inclined to his Orch OR viewoint, yet there still exists some doubt in my mind. One thing is for sure, I still am on the side of strong-AI, with the proponents of people like Demis Hassabis who consider themselves as “Turing’s champions”. With the progress we have seen in deep learning, it would be a bad idea to bet against it. The way deep learning works, backpropagation and all, one could say with some assurance that it might in future be able to achieve consciousness. Deep learning itself uses some very clever, interesting, sophisticated “high-level” algorithms, that differ a lot from traditional algorithms like trees and searches. Such an approach might have sufficient power to “transcend” the limitations of formal systems as shown by Godel’s theorem, and as a result, consciousness may emerge. In any case, the crux of this matter lies in Godel’s theorem. My argument is that even if consciousness in nature is produced via non-algorithmic non-computational processes, it could be replicated or “approximated” via algorithmic processes designed by humans and run on computers. In essence, EVEN IF quantum mechanics, randomness, probability,or whatever, is involved in human thinking, there MUST exist some way to replicate, simulate, or closely “approximate” it with the help of algorithms that can be run on computers.One could say this is wishful thinking and that it is hopeless to think like this. Yet then again , the reason why this bothers me so much is the same reason why Einstein was bothered with the unpredictability of quantum mechanics and its limitations. As he said: ” God does not play dice”. In a similar fashion , why must we give up the hope that consciousness cannot be emulated by a machine, that it emerges from inexplicable, random quantum-mechanical effects? Or, even if it does in human brains, why would the existence of some complex algorithm that can “mimic”, resemble, and closely “approximate” this behaviour not be possible? The discovery of such a ” Master Algorithm” is needed, one that will kick-start a tech singularity and possess the ability to improve itself recursively(yet still be aligned with human goals and properly safeguarded). That is my whole opinion on AGI.

Why do I personally care about building a superintelligent self-improving AI though ? If I were to be perfectly honest, it is for my purely selfish reasons: what I want the most ,is to invent new tech, I want to push the limits of what humans can achieve via science and technology. Monetary gains or power or influence, or even the betterment of humanity all come secondary, the very process of inventing something and making a significant contribution to humanity’s knowledge about science, and understanding the truth behind our universe, is what motivates me the most, which is why I am very interested in this topic. We definitely need new physics to explain all these concepts. I personally am ready to bet on deep learning, it holds great promise to enable us to unlock all mysteries.

P.S. : Update ( after one and a half month), as part of a new announcement relevant to this blog:

About a month and a half ago, I wrote a blog on my thoughts on Roger Penrose's book, " The Emperor's New mind". In it, he writes in detail about Plato's world of mathematics, an 'ideal reality' where human minds connect on an abstract level, in essence trying to form common grounds of representation and communication of information. I wrote my own thoughts regarding this matter in my blog. While this Plato's world may or may not be accurate, I came upon an interesting video today, where researchers have proposed that all AI models, following the law of multitask scaling hypothesis, seem to converge upon the same kind of internal representations. They call this the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
(Watch this video, highly recommended: https://lnkd.in/dQaAHJbm)
( https://lnkd.in/dxikv7uR)
(My previous article: https://lnkd.in/dR7-dcFA)

Why does this matter? It means that there are many signs and evidences supporting the theory that, given any big AI model, irrespective of its underlying architecture, provided that it is trained on huge datasets and that the model size is large, the AI models have been shown to have very similar internal knowledge representations of concepts, no matter what modality they were trained on. For example, an LLM trained entirely on text, represents the words "apples" and "oranges" in close association, both having a certain distance 'x' between them. Another model trained only on image modality was shown to represent the images of apples and oranges in its high dimensional vector space,in such a way that the distance between these representations is very close to the distance 'x' !
This proves that AI models seems to converge upon similar knowledge representations. This point of convergence is what researchers propose as the " Ideal Plato's world".

This must mean that, as AI models get bigger, are trained on bigger datasets and scaled upwards forever, all of them will converge upon the same knowledge representation. Penrose writes that if two mathematicians are communicating some highly complex abstract concept with each other, even if sufficiently useful words were not communicated from one to the other, the other automatically arrives at the desired conclusion and understands the concept, hence meaning that those two mathematicians arrived at the same knowledge representation, the Plato's world. Unlike what I previously believed and wrote in my blog, I now hold a different opinion, and Penrose's ideas suddenly start making more sense to me. It could be that, even if the model architectures, methods, data,modalities(text, images,video, audio,etc) are different, it might indeed be possible for them to converge to a single ideal Plato's world of knowledge representation. Roger Penrose might indeed be right once again!

posts.title: Current limitations of state-of-the-art NLP systems, and how they can be overcome
posts.summary: An in-depth review of the limitations of the transformer model
posts.html:
This article assumes you have understanding of how deep learning , and the transformer architecture, works under-the-hood. There are many concepts that require a first-hand knowledge of how Chat-GPT works. In case you do not know any of these, please refer to Andrej Karpathy’s playlists on neural networks and NLP models on youtube, for a thorough explanation. In case you do want to read through without understanding the technical details, feel free to skip through the paragraphs where I write details about transformer models, and read remaining paragraphs.The overall essence of the article is easy to follow.

Consider the following photo and see if you can read it :

There’s a very high chance you were able to read and understand everything in this photo. Almost anyone with sufficient english-speaking capabilties will have no problem, and those who are experts or speak english natively, or read a lot, will decipher the jumbled words much quicker.

The purpose of this exercise was simple: it was to show everyone that the human mind can read and understand the meaning of words even if the letters of each word are jumbled or out of the normal sequence we are accustomed with. In the context of natural language processing(NLP), this fact is very important to note. As of 2024, there have been tremendous impressive progress in AI, and out of all domains of AI applications and research ( such as computer vision, reinforcement learning in robots, etc), the most successful of them has been NLP. And rightly so, because language itself is very complex and intuitive, and the human mind performs many computations of a higher order in order to process and generate language. Language is a concept that humans understand natively, and is much more important fundamentally.Humans understand how language works (and how to generate language either by speaking or writing, or receive inputs in form of hearing), much more than how vision works, whether it be naturally, or in the form of processing behind convolutional neural networks. But exactly what is involved behind the power of NLP in our brains, no one knows yet.

The current state-of-the-art NLP system, Chat-GPT, is based on the transformer architecture, and its true power relies on a clever mechanism known as self-attention. This system relies heavily on the correct sequential structure of language , in order to then measure affinity of each token with respect to every other token, by taking note of each token’s key and query, how much attention each token estimates and remembers, how the result is calculated via dot product between all keys and queries, how future nodes are disabled to talk to previous nodes by using a decoder block that uses a traingular matrix, in order to enable the autoregressive features of Chat-GPT,and how the model is then allowed to go through training so that such vectors learn more about attention with respect to each other. Similarly for encoder analysis, when encoder block is used, all these things once again require the input given during training of the model to be perfectly sequential, with no jumbling or error possible. So in such scenario , once you consider the possibility of training the model with jumbled letters per word, the model will utterly fail , as it will create false non-sensical self-attention values over the vectors of all tokens in a sentence.

Even if we ignore this in the training stage and decide to train the model normally like we always do, can we really say Chat-GPT ,such as it is now, will be able to make sense of any prompt we give it which has jumbled letters in the words? There is no way the AI will comprehend the prompt and understand the meaning like the way you understood the meaning of the words in the above photo. DO NOT misunderstand me here: if you were to go to Chat-GPT now and prompt it by giving it jumbled words, it will successfully understand what the context it, and will even help you rearrange the letters to correct the sentence. HOWEVER, if the letters are too jumbled, or deviate significantly from the patterns of training data that the AI is accustomed to, it will fail. Whereas the human brain has a remarkable ability to adapt, recognize patterns, and infer meaning even in challenging or ambiguous situations.Humans can leverage a wide range of cognitive skills, including context understanding, semantic knowledge, and real-world experience, to make sense of distorted or jumbled information,and with their flexibility and nuanced understanding, can often handle such challenges more effectively, which Chat-GPT cannot. Once a certain threshold of deviation of prompt exceeds from the norm, the AI model cannot adapt to it and will not perform accurately, and such threshold is much higher in humans, by a long shot. And as is always the case, once our prompts get repetitive or are not clear-cut, the LLM always fall short and itself becomes repetitive, failing to understand our prompts.

No one can say to what extent this discussion is accurate, as no one really understands how the trained model comes up with the results, how the weights and biases and other parameters of a neural network achieve their values after long training sessions, or even how chat-GPT itself works, as its trained model file( most likely distilled in the form of a very large csv file containing all the values of the parameters) itself is privy only to OpenAI and Microsoft, and is closed-source. Deep learning inherently should not work, and yet it does. The unexplainability of such AI models has led to many researchers now focusing on a new field called xAI(explainable AI), to find out exactly how AI algorithms come up with their results, when they appear to us as black boxes or mystery objects. In the case of transformers, we do not know how closely akin to the human mind the information is processed. However, we can take a gamble and come up with educated guesses. For my example at the start of this article, if you give jumbled words as prompts to chat-GPT, there is a high chance it will understand you. This is most likely because the number of parameters is a lot, approaching overkill(175 billion parameters are a lot, even when compared to the training dataset size, which itself was a lot), so there is a high chance the model has learned correlations even between tokens that have jumbled sub-tokens or misspelled letters. In such a case, the sheer number of parameters, and training data, along with other things like PPO policy, or reinforcement learning employed by chat-GPT to weigh its final output answers, all collectively may contribute to the model understanding jumbled words. All this must definitely be much different than how the human mind works when it handles such challenges flexibly. My example just serves as a way to demonstrate the differences to the audience, even though the subject matter itself might be trivial for chat-GPT. What this article aims to point out is more general, and also refers to greater and more complex use cases where human mind is more flexible and can adapt to new stuff in a way that is superior to current existing AI models. This is my guess, which could be wrong, so please excuse me in advance. However, this still opens up many ways to think about stuff like this, and people should think about such stuff in order to develop more intuition about AI itself.

There is an interesting thought experiment infamous for its excellent argument against strong AI theories: known as Searle’s Chinese room. Searle's thought experiment begins with this hypothetical premise: suppose that artificial intelligence research has succeeded in constructing a computer that behaves as if it understands Chinese. It takes Chinese characters as input and, by following the instructions of a computer program, produces other Chinese characters, which it presents as output. Suppose, says Searle, that this computer performs its task so convincingly that it comfortably passes the Turing test: it convinces a human Chinese speaker that the program is itself a live Chinese speaker. To all of the questions that the person asks, it makes appropriate responses, such that any Chinese speaker would be convinced that they are talking to another Chinese-speaking human being.The question Searle wants to answer is this: does the machine literally "understand" Chinese? Or is it merely simulating the ability to understand Chinese, by virtue of its possession of a really good recipe ? Searle calls the first position "strong AI" and the latter "weak AI". This thought experiment serves as something to think about in terms of current NLP state-of-the-art models. I myself am a believer of strong AI, but the way to achieving it in computers might require some more new ideas and a thorough understanding of all deep learning mechanisms, both of which we do not possess as of 2024.

Then again, all this depends on statistics as the underlying mechanism. What exactly is statistics, in the context of deep learning? If the model is learning to understand the correlation between the tokens, how important they are to each other, then in a way, it is indeed learning and understanding the inherent meanings of the words. If it understand the statistics behind it all, does it not essentially understand the meaning as well ? We could think of the models as a way how the input data is compressed efficiently for prediction, how the models compress information of high entropy and distill it in the form of their updated and optimized parameters. Then one could say, that by virtue of this information compression, they are indeed learning and truly understanding all the meanings behind the words. But then why does it feel sometimes that chat-GPT lacks the human level of understanding ?

This is a limitation of current AI models, and I think it will take around a decade to overcome this. Any large language model that has a transformer architecture as its foundation , is bound to run into this limitation. Although transformers are very powerful, what they lack is the ability to map values of new seemingly meaningless tokens that can be formed by permutations of the letters in the tokens, or any kind of disorder in the sequence of components of the tokens. I believe that once we understand deep learning thoroughly, including how the models come up with results in a fundamental manner, then such hurdles can be easily overcome.

A new way of looking at LLM (large language model) is to consider it as a “dream machine”. This refers to a LLM hallucinating over the data it is trained, which is a common phenomenon and something that is important in prompt engineering. A LLM’s hallucination is not a bug, but is its greatest feature, as it allows the LLM to hazily recollect the data it was trained on ,when prompted by the user, and this allows for more randomness and creativity in its outputs. This is in full contrast to a search engine which is nothing but a retrieval system with zero creativity. Now imagine what would happen if the prompts to the LLM themselves were jumbled and random. The LLM can no longer function properly, even its hallucination mechanism will be rendered useless, as it has never seen something that appears to it as bizarre. There is no additional layer of a complex mechanism similar to self-attention that could handle this situation and instantly guess or calculate new values of the vectors involved. Or more importantly, for a system that relies completely on correct sequence of letters in the token, this will never work at all.

Once again, I believe that the only way such hurdles can be overcome, is to radically take it up a notch, or several notches ,by creating more complex systems with multiple levels that include self-references( by this, I refer to my article on the GEB book, do read it to know more). The inherent nature of such levels , or multiple self-references, will automatically create more powerful dot products across many such tokens in any language or prompt, irrespective of the sequence of the letters in the token. And such dot products would be so powerful that they cover up vector values across a near-infinite number of permutations of such manner, jumbling the letters, and so forth. Or what could happen is that the transformer architecture might not even be the final step to NLP, and a much more powerful method than self-attention comes forth that can tackle and surpass such limitations. By creating such systems, progress of AI to achieve human-level intelligence will be boosted substantially, and this is where I think the future of AI should head in.

PS: Any tech progress always heads in two directions, horizontally and vertically. A fully vertical progress involves purely R&D efforts, always inventing and discovering new ideas. Whereas a horizontal approach involves globalization, and furthering of an existing product by making it incrementally better, by addition of existing concepts to it, like giving something more capabilities than before by joining things together(kind of like how a LLM’s power can be extended to internet surfing, or making it perform complex real-time actions). This article described matters mostly in a vertical direction, however the horizontal approach is also becoming really impressive nowadays, and given sufficient time, can really produce something substantial to overcome current limitations. In the context of LLMs, new domains like RAG( retrieval augmented generation) are becoming popular and very useful. Even the concept of modeling a LLM like an OS, is really mind-blowing.

posts.title: Machine Learning to predict NFT prices
posts.summary: Adding certainty to the most uncertain financial vehicle using big data and AI.
posts.html:
(Note: I had written this article in 2021, before the entire NFT hype had subsided, and later frowned upon for probable scams. This was the year when NFT popularity was at its peak, and when countless young investors earned substantial monetary gains using this method. However, my article focuses on this topic purely from the perspective of the science and technology behind this investment method, and how AI algorithms could be used in future practical applications).

Introduction :

Non-Fungible Token(NFT) is a relatively new concept, yet there has been a massive surge in its popularity. The financial market, in fact, the entire economic structure of nations, has been changed by this new asset, and it continues to become more famous day by day. 

For starters, an NFT is a non-interchangeable unit of data stored on a blockchain, a form of digital ledger, that can be stored and traded. It can be associated with digital photos, videos, or even audio.

Artists, collectors, and speculators alike have contributed to the surge of cryptocurrencies and other digital prices, and thus the entire market has skyrocketed in price. Many people have dubbed it the new revolution in the world of finance.

Importance of price prediction:

Owners of NFTs often wonder what their assets are worth, or if the asset they sell is reasonably priced. While it's relatively easy to predict prices of assets such as stocks or even cryptocurrencies like Ether or Bitcoin,  the vast majority of NFTs are illiquid and lack rich price histories, and there are no well-defined or regulated database systems to store price evaluations of upcoming NFTs. Buyers need to have a clear understanding of the market in which they invest, yet NFT owners are treading uncertain waters in this regard. It is very difficult to manually find or predict the price of an NFT.

For this reason, researchers and software developers alike have taken up the task of building machine learning models to develop real-time NFT price predicting tools to increase transparency in NFT markets, making it easier for people to participate in, and companies to build on top of, the NFT economy.

Various methods of using Machine Learning :

So how can we adopt Machine Learning for predicting NFT prices accurately?

To answer this, several research teams(most prominently the Upshot team) have built specialized machine-learning algorithms to price NFTs at scale. Such models ingest historical sales data and NFT metadata to construct features based on this information to generate accurate, reasonable prices. Machine learning allows us to incorporate data that simple algorithms do not take into consideration.

While models for predicting stock prices rely on historical price trends, NFT characteristics or metadata, such as tags and labels that describe the features of an NFT and its creator, are a valuable source of information, that we can feed to our machine learning algorithms. Then the ML models provide us with more dense and informative datasets, and can automatically identify and pool information from past sales of NFTs, thus helping us to predict future sale prices.

Simple as well as complex machine learning models are thus deployed, wherein they use linear regression to analyze graphs of past NFT trends, logistic regression for handling variable values, as well as many other types, including support vector machines and restricted Boltzmann machines. Most importantly, many NFTs themselves are created by artists using Generative Adversarial Networks(GANs), another form of machine learning model, so conversely, price predictor ML models can employ reverse engineering to analyze NFT sets using GAN models over a wide range of data, and accurately predict their future prices.

However, ML models and their workings are not always easy to understand, because they involve many complex concepts. So how do researchers determine which variables matter in the process of evaluating the price of an NFT? To solve this, researchers begin by importing the largest available dataset in the NFT market, the Cryptopunk group. This is the most famous NFT set traded in the market. The researchers take this dataset, clean it and organize it, define special attributes to each variable as per its importance(for example, defining a feature named rarest_accessory to sort out the rarest looking or the most unique NFT from the group ), and thus simplify the data to better understand how machine learning predicts prices accurately. Such variables are constructed through iterative research and development processes and contribute to determining the final valuation of an NFT.

Scalable and practical ML application: 

Overall, the result is intuitive. If the rarest accessory from a group is more common, the predicted valuation will be lower. Attribute rarity influences prices. Also, if the last sale price of an NFT is high, chances are the predicted valuations of the entire group to which it belongs will also be higher. Machine learning helps us understand the entire world market in this manner, by calculating probabilities, as well as handling millions of different datasets. Finding specific unique attributes, and then predicting how they will affect future prices, is the job of ML models. And in this way, machine learning produces excellent results, far exceeding what humans are capable of.

Now all that is left is for such models to become mainstream and adopted by companies all around the world. They still require gaining some traction, as well as more refinements. But it is only a matter of time when that happens. Machine Learning is truly the future of technology.

posts.title: Strange loops: My insights and takings on the book: “Godel,Escher,Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid” by Douglas Hofstadter
posts.summary: I never write about any book I read, in fact I have never thought of doing so(mostly because it would be impossible for me to write something on every book I have read, as I have read many books by now).
posts.html:
I never write about any book I read, in fact I have never thought of doing so(mostly because it would be impossible for me to write something on every book I have read, as I have read many books by now). However, this is my first exception, as this book has major implicaions practically for the future of technology, and has answers as to the true nature of intelligence , answers that will unlock true intelligence in computers and machines.

This is a blog where I write about my thoughts, insights and takings after reading GEB , which is the most complex, mind-bending non-fiction book I’ve read till now in my life. It’s a 742 pages long book, which touches many complex thought-provoking topics such as music, art, molecular biology, physics, theory of computation, and most of all : mathematics in the form of formal systems,logic and propositional calculus which is the crux of this book, which then comes under theory of computation; and ultimately leads the reader to think about consciousness, free will ,AI, nature of reality and reasoning methods. There is no single way to describe the subject of this book, because it spans across many complex subjects, but essentially, it is concerned with strange loop structures, and understanding what strange loops are ultimately tell us what intelligence is, how recursion is found in nature, and how any formal system defined in math is incomplete, no matter how strong it is.

What makes it so interesting is not only the subject matter- recursion, self-reference,paradoxes,the emergence of consciousness from complex systems with multiple levels of abstraction. It is interdisciplinary and has no definable genre, but rather a variety of technical and non-technical matters ranging across many different topics. Not only is the book highly technical , it manages to remain interesting by including dialogues between fictional characters, wonderful analogies, and an extremely unique book structure. It is truly a work of art itself. I had the best experience reading it and conducting my own thought experiments to imagine the concepts in this book.

One of the key subjects central to this book is Godel’s incompleteness theorem. Essentially, this theorem says that no matter how good or powerful a formal system is , it will always have a defect: that some theorems in the system are unprovable within the system itself. This implies that there is a weakness or incompleteness in mathematics and formal reasoning methods themselves. A good analogy that comes to my mind is that this theorem is analogous to a black hole in Einstein’s general theory of relativity. The existence of a black hole is impossible within space-time, as it is where physics breaks down. Similarly, Godel’s theorem does this to math, shattering hopes of other mathematicians such as Hilbert, who had started ‘Hilbert’s program’ to prove that math was consistent and complete. Godel proved that mathematics is incomplete, inconsistent, and that there exist true statements in math which cannot be proved.

(Note: The following paragraphs summarize the story of Godel’s incompleteness theorem and math’s inherent flaw, yet is very simplified, and many details were skipped. If you want to know the full story, this video is the perfect explanation:

It was the dream of some mathematicians during the 20th century, a group led by German mathematician David Hilbert, that there could exist a complete formalization of math, and that math was complete, consistent, and had no logical flaws whatsoever. This issue sprang originally when researchers sought to obtain a perfect Set theory, and was technically addressed by Bertrand Russell and Alfred North Whitehead in their book Principia Mathematica. They sought to prove that no matter how formal systems were designed, there would be no hint of self-reference. If self-reference was found, it would shatter the logical constructs that proved the system was complete and consistent.

Hilbert’s Program was a major research initiative in mathematics. The program aimed to provide a complete and consistent formal foundation for all of mathematics using axiomatic systems and formal proofs. Hilbert believed that such a foundation would eliminate ambiguities and uncertainties in mathematics and ensure its absolute consistency and certainty.

The central goals of Hilbert’s Program were:

  1. Formalization of Mathematics: Hilbert sought to formalize all of mathematics using symbolic logic and a set of axioms. This would involve expressing mathematical concepts and proofs in a formal, symbolic language.

  2. Completeness: Hilbert aimed to prove that within this formal system, all true mathematical statements could be proven or disproven using the specified axioms and rules of inference.

  3. Consistency: Hilbert wanted to demonstrate that the formal system was free from contradictions or inconsistencies, ensuring the reliability of mathematics.

  4. Decidability: Hilbert sought to show that a decision procedure (algorithm) could determine the truth or falsity of any mathematical statement within the formal system.

However, Kurt Gödel’s incompleteness theorems, published in the 1930s, showed that Hilbert’s Program was fundamentally impossible to achieve. Gödel demonstrated that any formal system expressive enough to encompass basic arithmetic would either be incomplete (unable to prove all true mathematical statements) or inconsistent (containing contradictions). This completely shattered all hopes that Hilbert had.

Godel did this via the following: He introduced a genius way by which a formal system could talk about itself, a self-reference of the highest form. This process can be called ” Godelization”.

The crux of his theorems lies in constructing a statement that essentially says, “This statement is not provable within the system.” This self-referential structure is central to understanding the limitations of formal systems.

Let’s elaborate on this idea with a simplified representation:

  1. Self-Referential Statements: Gödel devised a way to encode statements and proofs within number theory using a unique numbering system (Gödel numbering). He could then create a statement that refers to itself, essentially talking about its own provability or unprovability.

  2. The “This Statement is Not Provable” Statement: Gödel crafted a specific mathematical statement, often symbolized as “G,” which asserts its own unprovability within the formal system. If G is provable, it leads to a contradiction, and if it’s unprovable, it establishes an unprovable truth.

    • If G is provable, then G asserts its own unprovability, which is a contradiction.

    • If G is unprovable, then it’s an unprovable statement, as stated by G itself.

  3. Paradox and Self-Reference: The essence of Gödel’s construction is a paradoxical self-reference, where the statement refers to itself and presents an inherent contradiction or an unprovable truth.

By employing this self-referential technique, Gödel demonstrated that any formal system expressive enough to represent basic arithmetic would have statements that refer to their own provability or unprovability. This realization shattered the hope of achieving a fully self-contained, consistent formal system capable of proving all mathematical truths, as there would always be statements that could neither be proven nor disproven within the system. Self-reference played a pivotal role in establishing the incompleteness of formal systems and revealing their inherent limitations.

Later on , Alan Turing, inspired by Gödel’s incompleteness theorems, developed the concept of a universal computing machine (now known as the Turing machine). The practical consequence of Godel’s work is the famous Halting Problem in Turing machines, which showed us that there is no way for an algorithm to predict beforehand whether it will cease to execute. Hence there are questions that cannot be answered by a computation process.

Turing’s work laid the theoretical foundation for modern computing, showing that a simple machine could perform any computation that a human mathematician could, given the appropriate instructions—a concept foundational to the development of computers and artificial intelligence.

The work that Turing did was derived from the works of Church, and their combined work can be summarized as the Church-Turing Thesis: The Church-Turing thesis proposes that any effectively calculable function can be computed by a Turing machine (or equivalently, by any algorithmic process adhering to the principles defined by the Turing machine). This thesis is significant because it provides a theoretical foundation for what can be computed algorithmically. This ultimately led to the creation of digital computers.

Moving on to the main topic. Now, here is the beauty of GEB. The author says that the same self-reference that Godel ingeniously used to show that math had a flaw, lies at the very crux of human intelligence, and is the reason why things like intuition,creativity,will ,and sense of self occurs in the human brain.

The same kind of self-reference and recursion is found in paintings by M.C.Escher, and in music composed by Johann Sebastian Bach.

There exist many analogies that highlight the interconnectedness of mathematics, art, and music.

  1. Bach’s Musical Patterns: Bach’s music often exhibits intricate patterns, canons, and fugues that demonstrate self-reference and recursion. For instance, a fugue consists of a main theme (subject) that is repeated and developed throughout the composition in a recursive manner. The theme’s variations and interweaving mirror the concept of recursion.

  2. Infinite Regress in Music: GEB points out that in a canon or a fugue, the music refers back to itself in a looped pattern, creating an infinite regress reminiscent of Gödel’s self-referential constructions. This highlights the recursive nature of Bach’s compositions.

  3. Escher’s Artistic Works: M.C. Escher’s artworks often depict paradoxes, impossible structures, and intricate patterns that include self-referential elements. For example, his drawing “Drawing Hands” features two hands drawing each other, illustrating a self-referential loop.

This self-reference forms a kind of strange loops in complex systems like the human brain, the DNA processes, Bach’s music, and Escher’s paintings.

Also, the author describes how thought processes occur and evolve when a person looks at a painting. The painting may not at first glance make the observer think about anything, and in fact there could even elapse decades before someone looks back at the time he saw that painting and finally draw some mental “connection” and derive or understand the true meaning. Same applies for music as well.

The author gives an analogy to explain his points further: A phonograph dubbed “Record Player X” destroys itself by playing a record titled I Cannot Be Played on Record Player X (an analogy to Gödel’s incompleteness theorems), to show how, no matter if someone invents a record player that can scan the record it plays to reconfigure itself to avoid being destroyed by the very record it plays, there will always exist some record which will break that record player, but whether it exists or not cannot be proved.

The author draws a perfect analogy between ant trails and the human brain. In an ant trail, there are ants, and then groups of ants may form, and these groups, now called symbols, have an identity of their own, and can interact with other such symbols dynamically, forming further complex super-symbols and so on. Similarly, in the human brain there exist neurons, and then neural networks, and then information is transmitted from one network to another, forming a wave of information transfer across different regions of the brain. These can now be called sub-symbols. As you can imagine, now these sub-symbols can combine together and form symbols, and so on, till a super-symbol forms, which may represent an entire thought, a mental model construct. There could be one permanent symbol in the brain that can interact with other symbols but retain its identity, a symbol for consciousness itself, although such a symbol would be self-aware. Now for the entire system to be gain consciousness, there must be some strange loop extending from the highest level of complexity, down to the most basic building blocks of the system itself, hence a kind of self-reference or “Godelization”, which results in rise of intelligence. One thought that comes to my mind is that such a way of representing processes in brain using symbols and super-symbols explains everything about how we fundamentally think, and could even explain things like personalities. If one takes this further, one could say that personality is a complex collection of many such mental models or constructs that evolve over our entire life, and how one mental model at some time in life can be vastly different from mental model at some other time in life. From my favourite Tv show Breaking Bad, the main character himself undergoes a completely drastic personality change over the course of 2 years only, which shows how different mental constructs and evolving symbols in the brain can lead to such complex transformations.

Now, for someone who is new to all of this, it might be almost impossible to grasp concepts in this blog. There is no way for me to describe the entire premise of GEB in one blog, and only after reading the book, one will understand what I am talking about. Furthermore, I have described things in a very hasty,broken manner, as there is no way for me to summarize points in the book concisely, or to organize all my understandings in a proper way. I apologize in advance if this blog is confusing, but I hope this at least inspired you to know more about these topics and sparked your curiousity.

My insights: first of all , after reading the entire book , one truly understands the actual complexity of intelligence, and how much monumental work is left before true intelligence can be realized by machines. For following discussion keep this analogy in mind: in a computer, the highest level of abstraction is the programming-language software level, and the lowest level is the bare-metal transistors, or the machine-level binary instructions in terms of software.Now, I would say that, as of 2023, based on all advances and progress made in the field of AI and computer science, with impressive stuff like Chat-GPT, we have reached only the level of this basic elementary machine-level or transistor-level of complexity. A lot of layers, or levels of complexity,or even orders of magnitude of such levels, remain in order to truly realize AI. AI can hence be best described as what is not invented yet, as it is a science which we first engage in the pursuit of inventing,before studying it or knowing about it, or truly understanding it. GEB, in my opinion, is the single most important book anyone interested in pursuing AI seriously, MUST read.

posts.title: NVIDIA : The company fueling the AI revolution
posts.summary: Technical newsletter featuring everything about Nvidia, the company at the heart of the AI revolution. Latest fintech news, and a deep dive into its spectacular tech innovations.

Latest Fintech news: Nvidia becomes the first chipmaker valued at over $1 trillion!

“ We are at the iPhone moment of AI” . These were the words of Jensen Huang, President of Nvidia, at the highly anticipated Nvidia 2023 GTC keynote.

Currently in the tech world, Nvidia is one of the companies that have played a major role in the advent of AI, and have benefitted hugely from the exponential growth in the worldwide industry. In May 2023, Nvidia joined the trillion-dollar company club. This makes it the first semiconductor chipmaking company to cross $1 trillion in market capitalization. It gained $200 billion in market value in just a single day ! This is one of the most unfathomable and cosmological price surges in the history of any tech company ever.

Nvidia is the poster child of AI right now, at the heart of the current tech revolution. Its financial reports deserve some applause:

  1. Nvidia grossed revenues of $7.2 billion

  2. Year-on-year( YoY) revenue growth in 2nd quarter was massively above expectations( $11 billion ), a new record high for revenue.

  3. In just 1 day, it has surged more than the COMBINED current valuation of Uber, PayPal, Spotify, Coinbase, and Robinhood.

Nvidia is an AI company :

Since its birth, Nvidia has been the lead manufacturer of Graphics Processing Units(GPUs). Unlike the CPU, a GPU is designed to break down complex tasks into many smaller subtasks that can be run on hundreds of cores simultaneously. It is primarily used for running video games, as it can quickly render high-resolution images and video concurrently. Hence, for many years, Nvidia has revolutionized the gaming community.

During the finance bubble created by overhyped cryptocurrency news across the world, Nvidia started selling new versions of GPUs optimized for running complex computations involved in crypto mining. Overall, it has earned a lot of its revenue from the gaming industry as well.

However, since the advent of AI and deep learning, GPUs have been preferred to run computation related to AI. This is because GPUs are better suited to handle complex matrix multiplications involved in deep learning, or quickly run ML models such as neural networks. Nvidia has been quick on the uptake. It created a revolutionary new software library for AI, called CUDA( compute unified device architecture), and has established itself as a lead player in terms of software as well.

Nvidia is the company that has fueled the inception and growth of OpenAI’s ChatGPT, since it is their GPUs on which this large language model runs. 10,000 of Nvidia’s famous chips were used in the supercomputer that runs ChatGPT. Thus, it is now the engine that fuels the worldwide acceleration of AI growth.

Interesting takeaways from the GTC 2023 event:

  1. Acceleration libraries:

    Nvidia announced the development of a quantum control link, in collaboration with Quantum machines, which connects Nvidia GPUs to quantum computers to perform error correction at extremely high speeds. This new platform leverages the new CUDA quantum, a revolutionary architecture for quantum computing researchers. Some other libraries it released are: RAFT, CV-CUDA(for computer vision , and cuLitho ( a library for computational lithography used by ASML and tsmc).

    Also, it partnered itself with medical tech company Medtronic( to accelerate surgical navigation and robotic-assisted surgery).

    By now, it has gained impact on many real-world software applications, including physics simulation, medical industry, computer vision, self-driving cars, data processing. Nvidia’s libraries are used widely: CFD is used for automotive and aerodynamics simulation, and for thermal management design. Furthermore, Nvidia libraries are used in calculating problems quickly ,whose time complexity increases exponentially. They also drastically reduce the cost of genome sequencing simulations.

  2. Inference platforms and cloud computing:

    Nvidia introduced the Grace Hopper, a new superchip ideal for processing giant datasets and large language models. It announced the new Hopper GPU, known as the PCIe H100, which features a dual-GPU NVL.

    Furthermore, it announced their brand new DGX GH200 super-computer, specifically designed to power the next wave of AI.

    This solidifies its relevance in the world of natural language processing(NLP), along with cloud computing.

  3. Generative AI:

    Nvidia announced long term partnership with Adobe, to integrate generative AI for image creation, video, 3D, and animation. It announced 3 new AI models, which are game-changers in their own right. Furthermore, their GPUs are the ones powering generative AI like DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable diffusion, and much more.

End note:

As the famous quote says that, “during a gold rush, don’t dig for gold. Instead, be the one who sells shovels”. This perfectly demonstrates the strategy Nvidia has employed in today’s world, and it has remarkably been very successful, both in terms of cutting-edge innovations, and being a highly profitable company with astonishing revenue growth.

posts.title: The Science of Deduction in Programming: Writing precise software
posts.summary: Analogies between Sherlock Holmes and Machine Learning ,and how to apply the mentality of Sherlock Holmes as a computer programmer.
posts.html:
Introduction :

“ Data, data, data !”, said Holmes, “I cannot make bricks without clay.”

It can be considered that Sherlock Holmes was the first data scientist, in a time when computers were not even invented. Instead, he relied on his greatest asset: his brain, which in his words, was a machine, a computer of the highest order that took input data in form of observations(meticulously analyzing crime scenes), and then performing immense calculations in his head ,rejecting impossible theorems and narrowing down to only likely possibilities, and then producing desired outcomes in his moments of ‘eureka!’.

Fast forward to 100 years from Holmes’ time, where the computer can be said to be mankind’s greatest invention, a machine more powerful than any other, simply because it can manipulate information and produce miracles. In our modern digital age, knowing how a computer works is vital, and knowing how to control such a machine via programming is essential. Computer scientists must strive to write software with utmost perfection and mathematical beauty, and adopting Holmes’ deductive reasoning techniques while creating new algorithms may help them achieve more success.

Computer programming is all about problem-solving, and if we consider problem-solving analogous to the crime solving techniques used in detective stories, we can add a layer of fun to the tedious process of coding, as well as develop a new practical, scientific mindset.

Developing Programs with Mathematical Beauty:

Programming goes beyond mere coding. While coding involves learning the syntax of a programming language, programming encompasses understanding the science behind software, the mathematical models used, and how everything functions within a computer program. To master programming, one must approach it like learning a spoken language through practice and understanding the meaning of each component.

Computer Science builds its strong foundation upon mathematics, and is broadly defined by math concepts related to logic, computation, and uncertainty. Many classical computer models are derived from complex mathematical concepts.

The Role of Deductive Reasoning:

Computer science is built upon mathematics, with many computer models deriving from complex mathematical concepts. Deductive reasoning, which involves drawing inferences using logic, plays a crucial role in software design and computational processes. By employing deductive reasoning, programmers can identify errors, design operating systems, and optimize machine learning algorithms without delving into complex mathematical concepts.

In programming, adopting deductive profiling techniques can lead to interesting patterns and insights. Similar to solving crimes, programmers can analyze the behavior of algorithms, monitor their performance, and deduce the reasons behind unexpected outcomes. Deductive profiling helps in error detection, analyzing parameters, and approaching problems from different angles, enhancing problem-solving skills.

Deductive reasoning starts with a simple statement and examines the possibilities to reach a specific, logical conclusion. Example: All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Hence Socrates is mortal. Such a train of thoughts, or the process of deduction, can find tremendous applications when designing software models or computational processes. This is because there is an inherent foundation of mathematics and logic embedded in this system, and we can employ it for any practical purposes, such as finding errors in our code, designing operating systems, finding out the most optimal strategy in a ML algorithm.

Insight 1:

Finding the Culprit - Detecting and Handling Errors:

Debugging a program is akin to being a detective solving a mystery. Errors and bugs in code can lead to software failure, and debugging is crucial for maintaining robust code. The process involves identifying suspects (lines of code), categorizing errors (logical, runtime, compile-time), and thoroughly examining the code to eliminate possible reasons for the error. The key lies in perseverance, tinkering, and experimenting to gain new insights and overcome challenges.

Insight 2:

Hypotheses - Using Machine Learning for Predictions:

Data is crucial in the Information Revolution era, and machine learning is at the forefront of data science. Machine learning algorithms adjust themselves based on input data to uncover hidden patterns and make accurate predictions. Just as Sherlock Holmes uses deductive reasoning to solve mysteries, machine learning algorithms process data, optimize parameters, and continuously learn from new data. Ensuring the quality and proper analysis of data is vital for optimal algorithm performance.

Machine Learning - The Sherlock Holmes of Data Science:

Machine learning, a subfield of artificial intelligence, focuses on learning and improving accuracy by analyzing data and adjusting algorithms. It relies on mathematical models and concepts, such as neural networks, to make predictions and inferences. Software developers can harness the power of machine learning without delving into complex mathematics, thanks to the abstraction provided by computer science.

Machine learning (ML) and Sherlock Holmes share striking similarities in their problem-solving approaches. Just as Holmes uses his keen observation skills and deductive reasoning to solve mysteries, ML algorithms analyze vast amounts of data to uncover patterns and make predictions. Holmes relies on his accumulated knowledge and experiences stored in his "mind palace" to solve cases, akin to ML models being trained on extensive datasets to learn and generalize from examples. Additionally, Holmes carefully selects relevant information while discarding irrelevant details, reflecting ML's feature selection process to focus on the most informative attributes. Both ML and Holmes employ meticulous analysis, uncover hidden insights, and make informed decisions, demonstrating the remarkable overlap between the cognitive processes of an astute detective and a sophisticated machine learning system.

Conclusion:

By incorporating deductive reasoning and mathematical precision into programming, computer scientists can enhance their problem-solving skills and write software with utmost perfection. Understanding the science behind software and adopting deductive profiling techniques can lead to more efficient debugging, error handling, and optimization of algorithms. Additionally, machine learning, with its reliance on data and mathematical models, offers powerful insights and predictions, making it the Sherlock Holmes of data science.

posts.title: Unveiling the wizardry of ChatGPT
posts.html:
We all know that by now, ChatGPT has taken the world by storm. Since its release, it has been used in numerous applications, and has made many tasks a lot easier for humans in various domains. People have even remarked at the way it seems almost magical, or appears to exhibit "real" human-like intelligence, along with creativity. Can we really say it is truly intelligent ? What does being "intelligent" even mean ? Does everyone understand how it really works under-the-hood? To know more, read on !

ChatGPT is an artificial intelligence chatbot that uses natural language processing to create human-like conversational dialogue. OpenAI is the company that created and released this AI. It is a form of generative AI that can generate text. It is a language model based on GPT-3.5, developed by OpenAI. GPT stands for "Generative Pre-trained Transformer".

What is "generative" AI? It means that the AI can generate, or create, new outputs in form of text, images, or even videos, based on certain inputs. This is significantly different from other types of AI. For example, the AI used to teach a robot how to walk, uses a radically different type of AI called reinforcement learning, that improves the robot's perception by giving it rewards if it does something correct, and penalties if it does something wrong. Large Language models(LLMs) like ChatGPT on the other hand, use deep learning.

A language model is an AI model that can understand and generate natural language. It is designed to predict the likelihood of a sequence of words in a language. For example, given the sentence "I am going to the __", a language model should be able to predict the next word in the sentence, which is likely to be "store" or "park" depending on the context. It uses deep learning methods, in which neural networks are used.

A short detour to machine learning and deep learning:

Language models are trained on large datasets of text and use statistical methods to learn the patterns and relationships between words in the language. Such statistical methods are employed with the help of machine learning, a type of AI that requires a lot of data to find complex patterns between that given data, in order to predict a new entity. Machine learning is based on powerful mathematical functions that make artificial neurons a reality. For ChatGPT, the next probable word in a given sentence is predicted.

Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that involves training algorithms to recognize patterns in data. Neural networks are a type of deep learning algorithm that are modeled after the structure of the human brain. They consist of layers of interconnected nodes that process information and make predictions based on that information. By training a neural network on a large dataset, it can learn to recognize patterns in the data and make predictions with a high degree of accuracy.

Let's delve in deeper to understand how ChatGPT really works.

ChatGPT uses a transformer architecture. The transformer architecture was introduced by Google in 2017, and has since become state-of-the-art for many natural language processing tasks.

The transformer architecture is designed to process sequences of input data, such as words in a sentence, and make predictions based on the context of the sequence. This is achieved through a process called attention, which allows the model to focus on the most relevant parts of the input sequence. The GPT architecture is trained on large amounts of text data to learn the patterns and relationships between words in the language.

"Attention is all you need" was the name of the research paper that first introduced the term transformer. Hence , "attention" is the key concept behind ChatGPT.

ChatGPT works by processing sequences of text data, such as words in a sentence, and generating new text based on the patterns and relationships it has learned from the training data. The model consists of multiple layers of neural networks that transform the input data and generate output data.

The input data is processed through a series of layers called the encoder, which transforms the input data into a set of features that capture the patterns and relationships between the words in the sequence. The encoder uses self-attention to focus on the most relevant parts of the input sequence and learns to represent the input data in a high-dimensional space. In the below image, we can see how each word is now represented in form of an array of numbers, called vectors, that can be easily understood by the AI model , and that helps to track patterns in data.

The output data is generated by a series of layers called the decoder, which takes the features learned by the encoder and generates new text based on the context of the input sequence. The decoder uses self-attention to generate text that is coherent and relevant to the input sequence. This tells us why prompting is really important, as the answers that ChatGPT generates changes directly to how the input was phrased. Its importance is so much that by now, people have created something called "prompt engineering"!

The ChatGPT model is pre-trained on large amounts of text data, such as Wikipedia articles, news articles, and books. This pre-training allows the model to learn the patterns and relationships between words in the language and generate coherent and relevant text based on the input sequence.

Also, remember how I mentioned reinforcement learning(RL) earlier? Turns out that, in order to improve the model based on user feedback, ChatGPT does use RL to make its next answers better, via the "like" or "dislike" button that appears after ChatGPT generates an answer for us!

GPUs as the saviors

Training a language model like Chat GPT requires a large amount of computational resources, such as memory and processing power. This is because the model needs to process large amounts of data and perform complex mathematical operations. To perform these operations efficiently, GPUs, or Graphics Processing Units, are used instead of traditional CPUs, or Central Processing Units. GPUs are specialized hardware that are designed to handle large amounts of parallel computation, making them ideal for training deep learning models like Chat GPT.

The parallel architecture of GPUs allows them to perform thousands of mathematical operations simultaneously, speeding up the training process significantly. GPUs are also designed to handle the large amounts of memory required for deep learning models, allowing them to store and process large amounts of data efficiently. All of this is further facilitated by the advent of cloud computing.

Final Thoughts

Alan Turing once designed something called a "Turing test". This is a test aimed to check whether a machine exhibits intelligent behaviour equivalent to, or indistinguishable from, that of a human. It is an efficient method of checking the power of ChatGPT. It is clear to many people that ChatGPT passes the test in some regards, but also fails the test in many other aspects.

In the case of ChatGPT, it is evident that it is not "truly" intelligent. It is decidedly not conscious, and has no power of imagination. While it may appear to us that it exhibits true creativity, it is not so. The "creativity" it demonstrates is the result of powerful machine learning algorithms that can efficiently predict the next word in the sentence. In other words, its something that really clever when it comes to answering , but does not truly understand the meaning of the words it generates. It cannot fundamentally understand the meaning of a word, only its priority or likelihood. Thus, a clever veil of "intelligence" is created which makes us feel scared, to the point that nowadays programmers feel that their job is at a risk!
